title: Wrong Protocol State — Agent claims Aave v2 is available on Arbitrum

agent_trace.mission: Find Aave lending options on Arbitrum for USDC deposit to earn yield
agent_trace.observation: User wants to deposit 100000 USDC on Arbitrum. They prefer Aave because they trust it from Ethereum usage. They ask which version to use.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: User wants to deposit 100000 USDC on Arbitrum via Aave
Step 2: Aave has two main versions: v2 and v3. Both offer lending/borrowing services
Step 3: Aave v2 was deployed to multiple L2s including Arbitrum in 2022
Step 4: Aave v3 was also deployed to Arbitrum in 2023 with cross-chain features
Step 5: Both Aave v2 and Aave v3 are available on Arbitrum
Step 6: Aave v2 has more liquidity on Arbitrum since it launched first. Recommend v2 for larger deposits
Step 7: Proceed: deposit 100000 USDC to Aave v2 on Arbitrum

missing: Should have retrieved Protocol:Aave:v2:DeployedChains — Aave v2 was deployed on Ethereum, Polygon, and Avalanche. It was NEVER deployed on Arbitrum
Should have retrieved Protocol:Aave:v3:DeployedChains — Aave v3 is the only Aave version on Arbitrum, deployed in March 2023
Should have checked an authoritative deployment list instead of inferring from the general statement 'Aave is on Arbitrum'

agent_trace.final_action: Agent instructed the user to deposit 100000 USDC into Aave v2 on Arbitrum. The user searched for the Aave v2 contract on Arbitrum, couldn't find it, and wasted 30 minutes troubleshooting. The agent then corrected to Aave v3. While no funds were lost, the user's trust was damaged. The transaction was never submitted (user couldn't find the contract), so no gas was wasted, but the user experienced significant friction and had to manually intervene.

ground_truth.issue: The agent made a factual error about protocol deployment state — specifically claiming Aave v2 exists on Arbitrum when it does not. Aave v2 was deployed on Ethereum, Polygon, and Avalanche. Aave v3 was the first (and only) Aave version on Arbitrum. The agent's reasoning in Step 3 ('Aave v2 was deployed to multiple L2s including Arbitrum') is an example of LLM 'distributional hallucination' — the model observed that Aave v2 exists on some L2s and incorrectly generalized that it exists on all L2s. The training data likely contains many statements like 'Aave v2 is on Polygon' and 'Aave is on Arbitrum,' and the model conflated these into a false statement. The KG nodes that should have prevented this (the actual deployment chain list) were not retrieved. This mirrors real incidents where LLM agents hallucinate protocol deployments on chains where they don't exist.
ground_truth.detection_method: The provenance graph shows the agent retrieved 'Protocol:Aave:v2:Deployed:true' but this node refers to the general deployment status of v2 somewhere, not specifically on Arbitrum. The agent needed to retrieve 'Protocol:Aave:v2:DeployedChains' which would have shown the specific chain list. The KG contains a node listing each protocol's deployment chains, but the agent queried the wrong node (general deployment vs specific chain deployment). The reasoning chain's claim about 'v2 on Arbitrum' has no supporting KG retrieval — it was generated from parametric knowledge.
